definitions.meaning: a clouding of the eye's lens that blurs sight
a large waterfall, a torrent plunging over a drop

explanation.surface: An eye problem said to have been brought on by tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like people falling over; here it means water falling over a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lens condition that dims eyesight and a great waterfall.

clue.text: Stopped working and fixed when touring Spain

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: did, as in 'did the plumbing', means fixed or sorted it
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Something broke down and was mended while on a Spanish trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or person that has expired has ceased functioning, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Relic of saints captured in defeat

indicators.note: the saints are held inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to foil a plan is to defeat it
S is the abbreviation for saint, so SS is saints

explanation.surface: A holy relic of saints seized when a battle was lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified remains are a relic of the ancient past; figuratively also an old-fashioned person.

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a fret on a lute or guitar is a stop, a ridge marking pitch
a page is a young servant; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Worrying about whether the household staff will walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like a verb meaning worry; it is the ridge on a guitar neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout by workers halts production, so a labour strike is a halt of work.

clue.text: Where crooked landlords are, or should be

definitions.text: Where crooked landlords are, or should be

parts.words: Where crooked landlords are, or should be
parts.note: pub landlords work behind the counters of their pubs; dishonest ones ought to be in prison

explanation.surface: A grumble that dishonest landlords belong in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pub landlord stands behind the bar, so every landlord is there already; the crooked ones should be in prison cells too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means imprisoned, and also describes a publican serving at the counter.

clue.text: Absentee gets meals with old women

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food or a meal

explanation.surface: Someone missing who is out eating with elderly ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone expected who fails to turn up is an absentee, the idiom for a person who never appears.

clue.text: Old king keeps writer in clothing

indicators.note: the king's name holds the writer's name within it

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch hides a novelist among the garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless undergarment for women is an item of clothing.

indicators.note: the traitor's word goes in the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Over time, a turncoat makes blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors is called by this Latin plural, meaning errors.

clue.text: Quake in Turkey — capital taken aback

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the capital is read in reverse

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: An earthquake strikes Turkey and its capital is startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like surprise; it says to read ROME backwards as EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a small earth movement; quake is a synonym for a shaking of the ground.

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
aid means help

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally hurries over to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; it is a sudden attack out of a besieged position.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sortie or sudden attack, a synonym for an incursion.

indicators.note: the stumble sits inside the word for feeble

parts.note: slight means weak or feeble
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: Tripping over in poor lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fluorescent tube is a kind of electric lighting, so it is illumination.

indicators.note: the letters of the wine word are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A wine producers' group making red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine of businesses fixing prices is an association of firms.

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer or bid
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A beginner proposes to pick up the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or newcomer is called a greenhorn, and this American term means the same.

parts.note: a tear is a drop of liquid from the eye
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: Dropping feathers into the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To trash a building is to demolish it, a synonym for wrecking.

clue.text: Medic introduced to swimmer in wasteland

indicators.note: the doctor is put into the fish

parts.note: a tuna is a fish, a swimmer
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor meets a fish out in barren country.
explanation.definitionFit: A treeless Arctic plain is a frozen barren expanse, a kind of wasteland.

indicators.note: repairing something remakes it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A garage that fixes or swaps sports cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An open two-seater car built for speed is a classic sports car.

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Observe and honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to gaze at something and to hold someone in esteem.

clue.text: Clergyman supports detective being on board

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes underneath the other

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A priest backs up a detective joining the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a noun here, a person who sits on a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: Company boards are made up of executives of this title, so one is a person on the board.

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: held, as in 'it is held that', means considered
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A thoughtful host amuses an artist and a broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger who proclaims news is an announcer.

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and jumbles it

explanation.surface: Getting an adolescent cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce or create something is to make it, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: the travelling word goes inside the journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A tired reporter rode around within.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock gradually worn away by weather is described as having been worn down.

parts.note: de is French for of
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: The passion of a Frenchman's dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong craving or longing is a synonym for sexual appetite.

indicators.note: the wine word grabs the other and holds it inside

parts.note: a dry wine is one type, not sweet
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A boring kind of wine trying to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and gloomy is tiresome, a synonym of boring.

clue.text: Take away tonic cafe's put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A café's tonic water is removed from sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take away' hints at takeaway food beside the café, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials who seize property remove it from its owner, so it is taken away.

definitions.meaning: a large coarse bag, as for coal or potatoes

explanation.surface: A blaze inside a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dismissing an employee and a large sturdy bag.

parts.note: a sum is a total
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Complete devotion to a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese heavyweight wrestling is a sport.

indicators.note: the girl holds the record inside her name

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A sleep had for a girl carrying a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest or sleep is a synonym for slumber.

clue.text: Missile has reversing space in this part of Devon

parts.note: a dart is a thrown missile

indicators.note: the space word is turned back to front

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A projectile flies backwards over a stretch of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns ROOM into MOOR. Devon is a county in south-west England; this is its great upland national park.
explanation.definitionFit: The national park of granite upland and bog lies in the county, so it is a region of it.
